name: spawn_task
description: Spawn a subtask. Use await_result=true to wait for the result inline, or leave false for fire-and-forget background execution.

input_schema.description: Spawn a subtask. Use await_result=true to wait for the result inline, or leave false for fire-and-forget background execution.

timeout.description: Max execution seconds (clamped to server max)

frame_type.description: Cognitive frame for the subtask. If omitted, auto-detected.

await_result.description: If true, wait for subtask completion and return result inline. Default false (fire-and-forget).

model.description: Model to use for this subtask. If omitted, uses default background model. Use a smaller model for fast lookup/summarization tasks.

output_format.description: How the subtask should structure its final report. Optional; sensible default applied per frame_type.

success_criteria.description: What 'done' looks like. Optional; default 'summary directly addresses the task and is internally consistent'.

payload_schema.description: F062: optional JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 compatible) for the subtask's result payload. When supplied, the executor validates submit_final_report.payload against this schema; on mismatch the subtask retries (per F061) and ultimately persists final_outcome='validation_failed'. Accepts a JSON object or a boolean (true accepts any payload, false rejects).

name: schedule_task
description: Schedule a task for later or recurring execution. Provide exactly one of 'when' or 'every'.

input_schema.description: Schedule a task for later or recurring execution. Provide exactly one of 'when' or 'every'.

when.description: One-shot time: 'in 2 hours', ISO 8601, or natural language

every.description: Recurring pattern: 'daily at 8am', '30 minutes', 'every monday at 10am'

model.description: Model to use for this scheduled task. If omitted, uses default background model.

concurrency_policy.description: Recurring only: what a fire does while this schedule's previous run (its subtask, or a DAG it created) is still active. coalesce_if_active (default) and skip_if_active start nothing; always_enqueue starts another run.

catch_up_policy.description: Recurring only: slots missed while Nous was down. skip_missed (default) runs once; enqueue_missed_with_cap runs once per missed slot up to catch_up_cap (each run still passes concurrency_policy, so the extra runs only start with always_enqueue).

catch_up_cap.description: Most runs enqueue_missed_with_cap starts at once (1-25; default 3).

name: spawn_sync
description: Run a subtask synchronously (inline) and return a typed SubtaskResult containing status, structured payload, raw text, and confidence. Pass payload_schema to require the subtask's report.payload to validate against a JSON Schema; on mismatch the SubtaskResult will have status='validation_failed'. Use spawn_task for fire-and-forget.

input_schema.description: Run a subtask synchronously (inline) and return a typed SubtaskResult containing status, structured payload, raw text, and confidence. Pass payload_schema to require the subtask's report.payload to validate against a JSON Schema; on mismatch the SubtaskResult will have status='validation_failed'. Use spawn_task for fire-and-forget.

payload_schema.description: Optional JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 compatible). When set, the subtask is instructed to populate submit_final_report's `payload` field with data matching this schema; the executor validates the result post-hoc. May be a JSON object or a boolean (draft 2020-12 boolean-as-schema).

frame_type.description: Cognitive frame for the subtask. Defaults to current.

timeout_seconds.description: Max execution seconds (clamped to server max).

model.description: Model to use for this subtask. Defaults to background model.

success_criteria.description: What 'done' looks like. Optional; defaults to a generic check.

name: dag_create
description: Create a DAG to orchestrate subtasks and checks with dependency tracking. A node that only waits for a Claude Code job, a pull request or a file must be a 'wait' node, not a 'check' node (see the node type). You do NOT need to poll for the result: when the DAG reaches a terminal state its outcome is delivered to you automatically (F087), so create it and move on. Use dag_manage only when the user asks about progress mid-flight, to cancel or retry, or to look up a DAG whose delivery you missed or that finished before this session (dag_manage action='recent').

input_schema.description: Create a DAG to orchestrate subtasks and checks with dependency tracking. A node that only waits for a Claude Code job, a pull request or a file must be a 'wait' node, not a 'check' node (see the node type). You do NOT need to poll for the result: when the DAG reaches a terminal state its outcome is delivered to you automatically (F087), so create it and move on. Use dag_manage only when the user asks about progress mid-flight, to cancel or retry, or to look up a DAG whose delivery you missed or that finished before this session (dag_manage action='recent').

type.description: 'callback' runs AFTER its predecessors and receives their results as context — use it to interpret or act on what earlier nodes produced (point a context_flow edge at it). It accepts frame_type / model / timeout_seconds like a subtask. Requires NOUS_DAG_CALLBACK_EXECUTION_ENABLED=true; with the flag off a callback completes instantly without running. 'gate' currently auto-passes — it is a marker, not an enforced quality check. Note: 'tools' below is honored ONLY for 'check' nodes — on every other node type (subtask, callback, gate, fix) it is silently ignored. 'wait' waits for a Claude Code job, a pull request or a file (wait_for) and runs no model and no shell: the orchestrator checks the condition every completion_check_interval seconds (default: every tick; a pr wait at most once a minute) until it holds (the node completes, and its result says what was seen), can no longer hold (it fails), or timeout_seconds or max_check_attempts runs out (it fails). A node that only waits for a job, a PR or a file must be a 'wait' node, not a 'check' node: a wait costs no worker. In a DAG created by a background (internal_only) turn, waits and the built-in PR check are the only conditions allowed: any other completion_check is refused there. A wait node takes name, type, instructions "" (put any note in description) and wait_for, and optionally timeout_seconds, completion_check_interval, max_check_attempts and description.

timeout_seconds.description: Execution timeout in seconds (default: NOUS_DAG_NODE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, ceiling: NOUS_DAG_NODE_MAX_TIMEOUT). F087: now a REAL bound — a node still executing past this plus NOUS_DAG_NODE_TIMEOUT_GRACE_SECONDS is cancelled and failed, so size it to the work rather than leaving the default on a long job. For a 'check' or 'wait' node with max_check_attempts and completion_check_interval, the timeout is raised to cover its polls (interval x attempts + one interval; the result says so in a Note line) and the DAG is refused when that is above NOUS_DAG_NODE_MAX_TIMEOUT. For a 'check' node the raised value is also its worker's own run timeout.

stall_timeout_seconds.description: F064.1: max seconds without activity before failing this node. 0 = disabled for this node. Unset = inherit NOUS_DAG_NODE_DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT.

completion_check.description: Shell command polled each tick. Exit 0 = success, 1 = failed, 2 = still running. For work that ends in a pull request, use the built-in check 'python -m nous.dag.typed_checks pr <owner/repo> --head <branch>' (or --pr <n>), exactly as written: it passes once that PR exists and fails if it is closed without a merge. Give it a completion_check_interval of 300 or more. When the node launches a Claude Code job (claude-jobs/runner.sh launch) that opens the PR, have it write the job id to a file under the workspace (redirecting runner.sh launch's output into the file will do) and add ' --job-file <absolute path of that file>' to the same check instead of checking the job's status yourself: the node then waits while the job runs and fails when the job ends without the PR. Only this exact check counts as the PR check: a merged PR it names is the outside confirmation your work is scored on, and a job-status or gh check you write yourself earns nothing. A DAG created by a background (internal_only) turn may carry no other completion_check: wait for a job, a PR or a file with a 'wait' node instead. A pr wait on a separate node earns no score: to be scored on a PR, keep this check on the node that opens it.

completion_check_interval.description: Seconds between completion check polls, or between a wait node's polls (default: every tick; a pr wait at least 60)

max_check_attempts.description: Max poll attempts (completion check or wait) before node fails

wait_for.description: (type='wait' only) What to wait for; one of three kinds. job: {"kind": "job", "job_id": "job-20261027-101500-ab12cd34", "until": "completed"}: a Claude Code job (claude-jobs/runner.sh launch prints its id). until "finished" (the default) takes any final status, "completed" fails the node when the job ends any other way; a job whose process died counts as failed. pr: {"kind": "pr", "number": 810, "repo": "owner/name", "until": "merged"}: repo defaults to NOUS_GITHUB_DEFAULT_REPO; until is "merged" (fails if the PR is closed without a merge), "closed", "head_changed" (needs "head", the commit sha it waits to move away from), "checks_done" (every check run on the head finished; failed ones are named in the result; with "head", fails if the head moved) or "review_on_head" (a review on the current head, from a login starting with "reviewer" when one is given). GitHub errors never fail a pr wait, and it polls at most once a minute. file: {"kind": "file", "path": "research/out.md", "nonempty": true}: a path under the workspace with no hidden component (nonempty waits for content, or an entry in a directory).

parent_node.description: F066.1 (type='fix' only): name of the node this fix attaches to. Fires when the parent transitions to 'failed'. The matching 'on_failure' edge MUST point from the parent to this fix node — i.e. from_node = (this parent_node value), to_node = (the fix node's own name). Pointing the edge the other direction fails validation.

fix_actions.description: F066.1 (type='fix' only): allowed action vocabulary. Phase 1 dispatcher rules: incomplete/validation_failed errors → retry_as_is; timed_out → skip_and_continue (or mark_unrecoverable); other errors → skip_and_continue then mark_unrecoverable as final fallback. retry_with_amended_prompt only acts when NOUS_DAG_FIX_LLM_DISPATCH_ENABLED=true.

max_fix_attempts.description: F066.1 (type='fix' only): max fix attempts per parent failure. Default 1.

expected_modes.description: F066.1 (type='fix' only): declared failure modes for typed dispatch (Phase 2). Phase 1 ignores this field.
